ruling.reasoning: The driver cancelled and the app reason recorded is rider_no_show, so the case runs under NS-1 rather than NS-3 [F4][NS-0]. The trace settles every NS-1 condition: arrival confirmed by driver tap at 18:25:55 within 200 m (40 m, closest approach 38 m) [F7][F1]; continuous presence at the pickup for 310 s counted from arrival, at or above the 300 s free wait [F7][F3][NS-1]; and before cancelling the driver sent 2 in-app messages (first 18:26) and made 1 in-app call (18:27) [F5][F10][F13][NS-1]. Nothing in the driver's own words gives a reason of his own for cancelling — his messages say only that he reached and waited, and his statement says he waited over five minutes with no rider, then cancelled [F10][F11][F14]; the reason element is therefore met and NS-1 holds [NS-0]. The rider's complaint that he "never even called" is contradicted by the call log, which shows an in-app call at 18:27 not answered [F13], and the system record of the messages and call overrides that statement [F5]; in any case the rider's not answering does not displace NS-1. The $5.00 charge is the fee on record and stands [F8][F4][NS-1]. No prior no-show appears on the rider's record, so no repeat-offender flag arises [F18][NS-9], and the driver's single upheld no-show entry is a profile matter that cannot decide this case [F19]. The read of the whole chat record, driver statement and complaint finds no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so no safety escalation is required [F10][F11][F14][SAFE-1]. No refundable km arise in a no-show case (no RD-2 computation), so the amount is nil and the outcome is no_action.
